title: I Let the Hydroponic-NFT Clock Catch the Intern Who Pocketed My Numbered Cups

parts.text: I stepped into the NFT gutter at 6:06 a.m. and intern Cruz was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE GUTTER. FORTY MINUTES. CUPS STAY WITH THE SLOT. I was twenty-seven, greenhouse secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered cups. Cruz shrugged. "Interns are the nutrient." I photographed the board, the booking, and his leftover net pots on my numbered cups. Then I asked for the gutter log. At 6:14 the house pinged why Cruz's name was on my pots. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The house can see Cruz's leftover net pots on my numbered cups.

social.video_title: He pocketed my numbered NFT cups on my gutter — Part 1/2
social.description: NFT gutter, leftover net pots, a forty-minute clock he posted. I logged the cups. Would you have asked for the gutter log?

parts.text: Cruz called it cloning until the house asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the pot still. The cups went back to my numbered slot. Cruz ran a slot of his own and told the next intern atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: INTERNS ARE NOT THE NUTRIENT. I keep my cups on a labeled tray. Cruz brown-bags his clones. The gutter finally looks like a slot, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Gutter log, numbered cups, and a second line on the board. Was cloning ever my pots?
